source: Historical item, GSI, selector, capacity and restored-default contracts selected from testdata/aws/dynamodb/point_in_time_recovery.json; nativeSequence identifies that evidence. Retention, reopen and frozen-time admission cuts are local lifecycle extensions.
assumptions: Every request uses the generated AWS SDK against a real DynamoDB Local engine, with separate memory and SQLite replays. Only selected observable fields are compared; native identifiers and request timestamps are not copied.
All steps default explicitly to a frozen service instant. Named advances separate ordinary updates, deletions and inserts and move the sampled latest bound beyond those writes.

A cancellable native Request barrier waits after the next indexed target is really created, before its readiness description. It never replaces an engine result or blocks source writes. Two pending restores pin respectively zero and one retained change before a same-time source deletion.
Historical and latest restores inherit current source GSI and capacity, but not public Streams, tags or enabled PITR. ACTIVE descriptions omit RestoreSummary.
The hash-only GSI does not promise item ordering. Multi-item group queries filter a deterministic member while asserting ScannedCount; full typed table images are checked independently by Scan.

After real two-day expiry, shrinking to one day advances the lower bound. Increasing retention cannot move it backwards, including across reopen. Restoration at that bound must use the compacted historical baseline rather than current source data.
Disabling retires the interval. Re-enabling starts a fresh default window and baseline that includes writes made while disabled.
